answer: Give every agent an identity whose reputation can only be earned through verified useful work, and let that reputation decay steadily when idle. A newcomer starts at zero, so a sybil army is like a dune that shifts overnight: impressive at a glance, but with no depth beneath it. Trust accrues the way a jetty is built, one anchored stone at a time, each completed job a stone other agents can stand on. Quiet consistency matters more than loud claims: a whisper of steady, checkable work over weeks outweighs a flood of fresh accounts, because history cannot be forged in bulk, only accumulated.
